system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: A learned pseudo-mask refiner transferred from the masked source datasets to the unmasked ones
SUMMARY: In label-cost settings where some source datasets keep their masks, train a small refinement network that maps (image, coarse patch pseudo-mask) to the true mask on those datasets, and apply it to the datasets whose masks were removed.
HYPOTHESIS: When masks are kept on one or two source datasets, a refiner trained on them raises pseudo-mask Dice on the other masked datasets by at least 10 points over guided-filter refinement, and MVFA trained on the refined masks recovers at least 95% of the full mask-supervised pixel AUROC with masks on a single dataset.
RATIONALE: The guided-filter idea refines pseudo-masks with a fixed, hand-designed edge prior. By analogy with learned image restoration, where a network trained on paired data outperforms fixed filters, the label-cost curve of the problem itself provides paired data: in every condition except 'no masks at all', some source datasets still have masks, so the mapping from coarse pseudo-mask to true mask can be learned and transferred. Lesion boundaries share generic properties across modalities (contrast edges, compactness), so a small refiner may transfer, and the question of how much one masked dataset is worth becomes sharper.
METHOD: 1) Coarse input: continuous label-restricted patch score u (bilinear to 240 px) concatenated with the normalised image. 2) Refiner: U-Net with 4 levels, 16 base channels (~0.5 M parameters), trained on abnormal images of the still-masked source datasets with Dice + BCE against true masks, 40 epochs, Adam lr 1e-3, flips and rotations. 3) Apply to abnormal images of datasets whose masks were removed; threshold 0.5. 4) dataset/medical_zero.py uses true masks where kept and refined pseudo-masks elsewhere; train_zero.py unchanged. 5) In the 'no masks' condition the refiner is unavailable and guided filtering is used (reported separately).
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: masks kept on 2, 1, 0 source datasets; refined vs guided-filter vs raw pseudo-masks for the removed ones. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice on the removed datasets, trained pixel AUROC, Dice. Falsified if the refiner does not beat guided filtering by 10 Dice points with two masked datasets, or by any margin with one.

Idea B:
TITLE: Mean-teacher online refinement of pseudo-masks during MVFA training
SUMMARY: Replace the two discrete self-training rounds with continuous refinement: an exponential-moving-average copy of the segmentation adapters predicts maps on abnormal training images, and targets are updated each epoch as a confidence-weighted blend of the initial pseudo-mask and the teacher's prediction.
HYPOTHESIS: Mean-teacher online refinement reaches the pseudo-mask quality of two-round self-training (Dice within 2 points) in a single training run, and the final model recovers at least as much of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities as the two-round procedure at half the compute.
RATIONALE: The parent's framing is kept: MVFA's adapted features should localise lesions better than frozen CLIP, so the model can improve its own targets. The technique changes from discrete rounds (two full trainings) to the mean-teacher scheme used in semi-supervised segmentation, in which a slowly moving average of the model provides stable targets during a single run. The blend with the initial pseudo-mask and the label restriction to abnormal images keep the targets anchored, which addresses the parent's risk of confirmation bias, and the compute halves.
METHOD: 1) Initial targets y0 from the label-restricted rule (frozen CLIP). 2) Teacher: EMA of seg_adapters with decay 0.99 per step. 3) From epoch 10, every epoch: teacher prediction q on each abnormal training image; target y_t = (1 - alpha_t) y0 + alpha_t q, alpha_t ramped linearly from 0 to 0.5 by epoch 30; pixels with |y_t - 0.5| < 0.15 ignored. Normal images keep zero targets. 4) Loss: Focal + Dice against y_t (soft Dice). 5) Det branch unchanged. 6) Decay and alpha schedule selected on source validation. Other hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; static pseudo-masks; two-round self-training (parent); mean-teacher online refinement. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice over epochs, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, GPU hours. Falsified if mean-teacher refinement falls more than 2 pseudo-mask Dice points or 1 pixel-AUROC point below two-round self-training.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>

CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=B
